title: This Small African Mammal Builds Its Own Roads
subject: elephant shrew

scenes.text: This small African mammal builds its own roads.
It's an elephant shrew, and it clears paths through the thick undergrowth.
Then it patrols those paths, hunting insects along the way.
But the real payoff is speed. Elephant shrews have been clocked at 18 miles an hour.
If a predator shows up, the cleared path is an obstacle-free escape route.
A road, a hunting trail, an escape route. Built by a mammal with a nose like an elephant.

description:
This small African mammal builds its own roads.
Elephant shrews clear paths through the undergrowth, patrol them for insects, and use them to escape predators at up to 18 miles an hour.
Would you build yourself a road?
first_comment: Which animal would you most like to see sprint down its own road?
